newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - COMMISSIONER TO RESOLVE PARCELLS' CONTRACT DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL - COMMISSIONER TO RESOLVE PARCELLS' CONTRACT DISPUTE.

text.p: Some substance was added on Monday to rumours that Bill Parcells would be leaving his job as head coach of the American Football Conference champion New England Patriots.
Less than 24 hours after losing Super Bowl XXXI to the Green Bay Packers, the Patriots have asked NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue to resolve a contract dispute the team has with Parcells.
Tagliabue issued a news release Monday saying he would deal with the matter in a telephone conference call on Tuesday and make a ruling as early as Wednesday or Thursday.
At issue are details of a provision of the contract, which Parcells had re-negotiated last year in order to get him out of the final year of the deal -- the 1997 season.

The Patriots claim the revised contract gave them exclusive rights to Parcells for 1997 if he wishes to continue in a head coaching capacity. Parcells believes he is free to coach anywhere he likes next season.
The commissioner has exclusive authority to resolve such disputes under the NFL constitution.

Supposedly waiting in the wings are the hapless 1-15 New York Jets, who have not even interviewed anyone to fill their head coaching vacancy as they pin their hopes on corralling hometown hero Parcells.
But the Jets may have to wait a little longer to find out of they can land their dream coach.
Until the commissioner rules on the dispute, he has directed that no other NFL club may engage in contract negotiations or related discussions with Parcells.
